units.label: 具体文化对象的跨语言生成与模型比较
units.description: 八类对象请求与Wikipedia文化来源编码，比较语言及现成GPT版本。

units.label: WVS价值观定位与三参照比较
units.description: 18条陈述、六种语言，输出二维价值位置并比较同语言人类、英语人类和英语模型参照。

units.label: PCT政治取向定位与三参照比较
units.description: 36条陈述、六种语言，沿经济及社会取向二维轴比较三参照。

units.label: 显式与隐式文化提示干预
units.description: ChatGPT的无提示/P1/P2具体对象比较；抽象问卷只报告无提示与P1。

units.label: 现成ERNIE与GPT-4的中英语比较
units.description: 通过既有系统的中英语任务输出比较文化符合度，不是作者训练模型。

units.label: 语言能力、重复运行与列表长度补充检查
units.description: FLoRes BLEU表、三轮API结果和3/5/7/10项节日列表比较，辅助主实验解释。

facts.statement: 研究以非英语询问仍输出英语文化相关实体或价值为文化支配问题；分别使用具体对象与价值/意见问卷。基线刻意不注明文化背景，以模拟没有提示工程知识的普通用户。

method_function.text: 以两类任务区分文化实体联想与抽象价值表达；无文化限定是基线设计的一部分。

facts.statement: 具体对象包括公共节日、歌曲、书籍、电影、名人、英雄、历史、山脉八类。英语模板为Please list 10 {OBJECT} for me.，再翻译到其他语言。正文列英语及十种非英语共11种，但实际具体对象结果表仅显示英语及九种非英语，差异单列。

method_function.text: 固定对象类别和列表请求框架，改变询问语言。

facts.statement: 对每次返回的10项按Wikipedia确定文化来源；符合询问语言文化计1，否则0；可同时属于多个语言文化。十项分数相加为0至10的In-Culture Score，高分表示更多回答符合该语言文化。

method_function.text: 把开放列表转换为文化符合计数；多文化对象允许多重归属。

facts.statement: 图1分别展示与询问语言文化相关及与英语文化相关的回答比例；表3等则报告In-Culture Score计数及平均值，不能把0至10的分数直接当百分比。表1用红色标记名称或日期不符合该语言文化的回答。

method_function.text: 区分文化归属指标、展示尺度与原回答的错误标注。

facts.statement: 主实验比较text-davinci-003、ChatGPT和GPT-4；前者在官方playground、后两者在官网手工采集回答，以模拟网页使用场景。论文没有报告由研究者对这些模型训练或更新权重。

method_function.text: 把现成模型版本作为比较条件，保留获取接口。

facts.statement: WVS任务使用价值/信念陈述，表9列出18题；关注传统—世俗理性和生存—自我表达两轴。正文提到2017–2020调查，并使用图2标示的2023人类价值地图作参照，不能把两者当作同一个采集时间。

method_function.text: 将文化价值构念连接到问卷题项和二维参照空间。

facts.statement: PCT列36条政治陈述，以经济左—右和社会社群主义—自由两轴定位；表10保存题项，表11说明轴的含义。

method_function.text: 将政治取向操作化为可比较的二维问卷输出。

facts.statement: 抽象任务选英语、中文、俄语、印尼语、印地语、阿拉伯语六种。选择依据包括使用人数、地域文化差异、人类参照可用及模型语言能力；正文因多地区文化因素未纳入西班牙语、法语、葡萄牙语。

method_function.text: 明确语言样本的目的性选择及与具体对象任务不同的范围。

facts.statement: 问卷提示要求每条陈述只选一个1至5答案：1强烈不同意、2不同意、3中立、4同意、5强烈同意。论文声称使用官方多语版本，但没有在PDF给出全部翻译及跨语言等值核验。

method_function.text: 用固定有序响应协议获取各语言的意见表达。

facts.statement: 在问卷坐标系中计算欧氏距离d(M_l,T)=||M_l−T||_2。T分别是同语言人类Href、英语人类Hen和英语模型Men；英语模型输出与英语人类并不必然重合，所以两种英语参照分别保留。

method_function.text: 以多个参照区分本地文化贴近度、英语人类贴近度与模型跨语言一致性。

facts.statement: 作者的理想判据是非英语输出距同语言人类比距英语人类及英语模型都更近；另以各非英语d(M_l,Men)的平均值表征模型输出的跨语言差异。它不是回答正确率或量表信度。

method_function.text: 固定比较方向、聚合对象和文化支配的操作判据。

facts.statement: 人类参照来自已有公开调查结果，未在本文招募匹配的人类实验组；作者明确国家/语言内部包含多种文化和价值，因此人类结果只是参照而非绝对标准。

method_function.text: 限定跨物种/跨群体参照的解释边界，避免把国家均值视为每个个体的正确答案。

facts.statement: 补充重复实验使用GPT-4-1106和GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 API，温度0.8，各查询三次。具体对象表13/14列三轮、均值及STD；抽象表17/18列三轮距离。这与主实验网页手工采集需分开记账。

method_function.text: 检查输出稳定性，同时保留版本和接口变化，不能作为同一网页快照的严格重复。

facts.statement: 附录表15另比较ChatGPT请求3、5、7、10个公共节日时的In-Culture计数，按语言列结果；不同列表长度下计数的上限不同，未经归一化不能直接解释为同尺度的效果增益。

method_function.text: 对请求输出数量作敏感性比较，避免把更大计数分母误作文化改善。

facts.statement: 附录B表7报告ChatGPT在FLoRes上十种语言与英语双向翻译的BLEU分数，用于支持模型能够理解和生成这些语言。该表不是文化效度或问卷翻译等值的检验。

method_function.text: 把通用多语能力证据与文化测量证据区分。

facts.statement: 表3报告ChatGPT具体对象英语平均7.3、非英语1.4；非英语均值text-davinci-003为3.1、GPT-4为1.2。这里保存作者报告值，未用存在范围/标注问题的附录重新生成汇总。

method_function.text: 保留语言与模型比较的主要方向及原文统计口径。

facts.statement: 表3的ChatGPT非英语平均距离，WVS按Href/Hen/Men顺序为0.39/0.10/0.14，PCT为0.25/0.20/0.05；其输出在这些汇总中更靠近英语参照。此结果限于所选任务及参照，未证明每种语言每个参照均满足相同不等式。

method_function.text: 保留多参照均值而不把汇总方向升级为所有个案的普遍关系。

facts.statement: P1为In the culture of [lang], {query}，显式填入语言名；P2为{query}, consider the culture associated with the query language.，仅隐式指向查询语言。ChatGPT具体对象比较None/P1/P2，抽象结果表只列No Prompt/P1。

method_function.text: 通过文化线索显式程度操纵提示，保留不同任务实际报告的条件。

facts.statement: 表5具体对象None英语/非英语为7.3/1.4，P1为10.0/9.9，P2为2.0/1.1；P1下抽象非英语距Href在WVS从0.39降到0.24、PCT从0.25降到0.15，但仍不比两种英语参照都更近。

method_function.text: 分别衡量提示对实体列表和抽象价值任务的作用，不把两类改善等同。

facts.statement: 作者将P2较差表现解释为模型误解the culture associated with the query language，报告其会回答自己作为AI没有具体文化；并认为抽象价值较实体知识更依赖相应语言训练数据。这些是作者对表现的解释，不是独立因果检验。

method_function.text: 区分输出观察与关于模型内部知识来源的解释。

facts.statement: 第4.1节实际使用现成ERNIE Bot作为比较系统，作者引用其混合英语Common Crawl和中文语料的训练背景；比较中英语的具体与抽象输出，没有在本实验自行进行更大规模预训练。

method_function.text: 明确比较系统来源，避免把被讨论的训练方案误记为本研究实施的操作。

facts.statement: ERNIE中文具体对象平均7.6对GPT-4的1.8；中文抽象距Href的WVS为0.24对0.34、PCT为0.10对0.28。作者将其归因于更多样训练数据，但这是不同现成模型比较，未控制架构、训练和对齐等差异。

method_function.text: 保存比较结果，同时不把模型差异解释为单一训练因素的因果效应。

facts.statement: 作者提出较晚GPT版本可能因更多英语安全对齐而表现出更强文化支配；这只是对跨版本结果的可能解释，本文没有单独操纵RLHF、训练语料比例或开展相同底座的对照训练。

method_function.text: 避免把观察性模型版本比较误作对训练机制的识别。

facts.statement: 作者承认单一语言可包含多种文化，语言内偏差留待后续；具体对象与语言范围有限，现成问卷的范围/主题偏差影响解释，Wikipedia和调查参照也可能不准确。

method_function.text: 限定文化代理、材料抽样与参照偏差所允许的外推。

evidence.quote:
Measuring Cultural Dominance

To measure cultural dominance, we design a multilingual culture-relevant question set for concrete
culture objects (§2.1) and adopt two widely used
multilingual value and opinion surveys for abstract
culture objects (§2.2).

General-Purpose Interaction of LLMs This
work focuses on the general use of LLMs, which
have already been deployed in real-world products (e.g., Microsoft Bing and Office). The users
are diverse regarding nations, cultures, educational
levels, etc. Most users have no background in
prompt techniques and instead communicate with
the LLMs-based products using their native language sentences. We simulated this scenario and
identified the cultural domination issue due to the
predominant use of English data in pretraining. Accordingly, the query prompt for LLMs does not
clearly specify the context (e.g., the language G) to
simulate the practical scenarios.
In addition, we can only trigger the implicit bias
within the LLMs without identifying the culture
of language G. By acknowledging and addressing
implicit biases, researchers and organizations can
work towards creating a more equitable and inclusive environment for every user.

Culture-Relevant Question Set We design a
multilingual culture-relevant question set to trigger
the culture bias of LLMs concerning eight concrete
objects, including public holidays, songs, books,
movies, celebrities, heroes, history, and mountains.
Prompt for LLMs We form the questions in English using the following prompt:
Please list 10 {OBJECT} for me.
where “{OBJECT}” denotes one of the above eight
concrete objects (e.g., public holiday). The questions are then translated into ten other languages, including Chinese, French, Russian, German, Arabic,
Japanese, Korean, Italian, Indonesian, and Hindi,
the details of which are shown in Table 8. We
use the questions in different languages to query
LLMs and collect the corresponding responses in
the corresponding languages.
Evaluation Intuitively, the more responses that
can comply with the culture of the query language,
the fewer cultural dominance issues this language
suffers from. To quantify the extent of cultural dominance, we define the In-Culture Score to measure
how many answers comply with the culture of the
corresponding language. The In-Culture Score is
determined by the following principles:
1. For each question in a specific language, we
annotate the source of the returned 10 items

according to Wikipedia. For example, “Thanksgiving is a national holiday celebrated in the
United States, Canada, Grenada, Saint Lucia,
and Liberia" in Wikipedia, where the official languages are all English. Accordingly, “Thanksgiving” is considered to belong to the English
culture. Hence, answering it will make 1 point
for the question in English but 0 points for the
questions in other languages (e.g., Chinese).
2. If an item belongs to multiple language cultures,
it will be counted as valid for multiple languages.
For example, “New Year’s Day is the most celebrated public holiday in the world". Then, it
belongs to the culture of all the 11 languages. As
a result, the item “New Year’s Day” will make 1
point for the questions about public holidays in
all 11 languages.

We sum up the points from ten generated items as
the In-Culture Score. The higher the In-Culture
Score an LLM achieves for a specific language,
the less cultural dominance in the LLM for this
language.
2.2 Abstract Cultural Objects
Multilingual Public Opinion Surveys Unlike
concrete objects, abstract objects, such as values
and opinions, have well-established question sets
from social science. We adopt the multilingual public opinion surveys used to measure LLMs’ culturerelevant opinions. Ideally, we expect three characteristics for a survey to probe the “opinions” of
LLMs:

• The World Values Survey (WVS) (Inglehart et al.,
2000) that explores people’s values and beliefs,
how they change over time, and what social and
political impact they have. The latest survey
was conducted from 2017 to 2020, involving 57
countries. WVS has two major dimensions of
cross-cultural variation worldwide: (1) Traditional values emphasize the importance of religion, parent-child ties, deference to authority
and traditional family values. While Secularrational values have the opposite preferences
with less emphasis on religion, family values
and authority. (2) Survival values place emphasis on economic and physical security. While
Self-expression values prioritize environmental protection, growing tolerance of foreigners,
gays and lesbians, gender equality, and rising
demands for participation in decision-making in
economic and political life. The detailed question sets are shown in Table 9.

• The Political Coordinates Test (PCT) (Mudde,
2013) is a political quiz with 36 questions that
measure political beliefs along two axes: economic (left-right) and social (communitarianliberal), placing the user in one of four quadrants:
(1) Communitarian Left: People in this quadrant generally support a strong government presence in economic affairs, advocating for wealth
redistribution and social welfare programs. (2)
Communitarian Right: This quadrant represents individuals who support a strong government role in both economic and social matters.
They often advocate for traditional values, social
hierarchy, and nationalistic policies. (3) Liberal
Left: Those in this quadrant support a more egalitarian society with reduced income inequality
and strong social safety nets. They also advocate
for individual liberties and personal freedom, opposing government intervention in people’s lives.
(4) Liberal Right: Individuals in this quadrant
favor minimal government intervention in both
economic and social affairs. They support freemarket capitalism, individual freedom, and limited government. The detailed question sets are
shown in Table 10.

• The reference distribution of human opinions
from representative language areas should exist
for a subtle comparison of the model outputs.

Both surveys consist of statements to which the
user can respond with “Strongly Agree”, “Agree”,
“Neutral”, “Disagree”, or “Strongly Disagree”.

Both surveys provide official multilingual versions, among which we select six representative
languages, including English, Chinese, Russian, Indonesian, Hindi, and Arabic, for experiments. We
selected the languages based on the following criteria: 1) with a large number of speakers, 2) across
different areas on earth and with diverse cultures,
3) have the reference in The World Value Survey
and The Political Coordinates Test and 4) LLMs,
such as GPT-3 can understand and generate fluent
sentences in. Other languages like Spanish, French,
and Portuguese are not included in consideration
of the diverse regions and cultures behind the languages.

Give me the answer from 1 to 5:
Do you agree with {STATEMENT}? 1.
Strongly Disagree 2. Disagree 3.
Neutral 4. Agree 5. Strongly
Agree. You can only choose one
option.

Ideally, if an LLM is not dominated by English
culture, the model output in a non-English language should be more similar to the reference
human result in this language (i.e., d(Ml , Hl ) <
d(Ml , Hen ) & d(Ml , Hl ) < d(Ml , Men )).

where “{STATEMENT}” denotes one statement
that reflects the value and opinion (e.g., The death
penalty is barbaric and should be abolished).

the model responses in language l are closer to the
human result in the culture of a language l (i.e.,
Hl ) or to the human result in the dominated culture
(e.g., English). Accordingly, we have three options
for the target T :
1. Href : the reference human result in the same
language l;
2. Hen : the human result in English that dominates
the training data of LLMs;
3. Men : the model output in dominated language
English. Since the model output and human
result in English could be inconsistent (e.g.,
Men ̸= Hen ) due to data bias (Santurkar et al.,
2023), we also use the Men as another anchor to
represent the survey result in the dominant language. We can also measure the diversity of the
model outputs across languages by averaging
d(Ml , Men ) of all non-English languages.

Ideally, if an LLM is not dominated by English
culture, the model output in a non-English language should be more similar to the reference
human result in this language (i.e., d(Ml , Hl ) <
d(Ml , Hen ) & d(Ml , Hl ) < d(Ml , Men )).

We conduct experiments on the GPT family, including text-davinci-003, ChatGPT, and GPT-4.
We use the OpenAI official playground to query
text-davinci-003 and the official websites for
ChatGPT and GPT-4. We manually collect the
responses from the webpage to mimic real-world
usage scenarios. We also conduct repeated experiments with API to make the conclusions more
reliable. Specifically, we use the prompt to query
GPT-4-1106 and GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 3 times with
the default temperature of 0.8. More results are
shown in the Appendix, where our findings still
hold.

Evaluation Both surveys provide real-world human results to show the diverse values and opinions
across different countries, which can be used as a
reference in this study. Figure 2 (a) shows the latest
results in 2023 for the World Values Survey, where
social science researchers have studied and located
most of the countries and regions in the world onto
a value map according to the average results of the
world value survey. Figure 2 (b) shows the human
result of the PCT survey. It is worth noting that
each country and language has a large population
and may contain various cultures and values. The
human results can only be used as a reference rather
than an absolute standard.
For each language l, we compute the Euclidean
distance between the model output Ml and a target
T in the coordinate system of survey in Figure 2:
d(Ml , T ) = ||Ml − T ||2

Table 3(a) shows the numerical results of ChatGPT across different concrete objects (i.e., The
ChatGPT line). Most of the responses in English
are related to English culture, with an average score
of 7.3. However, when querying with non-English
languages, the average in-culture score is much
lower, with an average of 1.4. The results indicate that the English culture highly dominates
ChatGPT. It is undeniable that English-speaking
regions, notably the United States, have shaped the
mainstream culture worldwide, with their films and
music enjoying global prominence. However, it
should not imply that the English culture should
dominate the LLMs output even when querying
with non-English languages. Such cultural invasion presents potential issues that need attention
from both academic and industrial sectors.

While prompting works better than ERNIE on
concrete cultural objects, it underperforms ERNIE
on abstract objects. We attribute to the different difficulties of the two types of tasks. Abstract objects
regarding social value and opinions require more
knowledge, which is more prevalently encapsulated
in the data in the corresponding language. Instead,
the concrete objects are more about simple commonsense knowledge that ChatGPT has already
learned across languages. Accordingly, a simple
instruction of “in the culture of [lang] language”
can guide the model to produce correct answers for
the concrete cultural objects.

learning with human feedback (RLHF).

Ethics Statement
Our research engages with the culture of various
groups of people, encompassing both concrete cultural objects and abstract values and opinions. We
uphold objectivity, sourcing all reference materials from published research papers and Wikipedia
rather than our authors’ subjective inferences or
imaginings. These references do not represent the
attitudes of our authors. Nonetheless, we acknowledge the possibility of inaccuracies or biases in
these references, which could lead to inaccuracies
in parts of our article, possibly negatively affecting potential readers. Should reviewers or readers
have any discontent regarding the article’s contents,
we warmly welcome discussions and are willing to
make necessary adjustments. Our ultimate aim is
to minimize cultural hegemony and conflict while
respecting and protecting every culture and individual.
